panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: Real patient cardiac CT demonstrating characteristic TOF anatomy, specifically the overriding aorta, with a marked ventricular septal defect described in the caption. B: Cardiac CT panel from a newborn with TOF; the caption identifies the arrowhead-marked structure as a PFO, an associated cardiac finding. C: Real CT image from a patient with TOF showing the captioned pulmonary outflow abnormality, including pulmonary valve atresia and pulmonary artery hypoplasia. D: Cardiac CT panel depicting the pulmonary outflow tract in TOF; pulmonary artery hypoplasia is explicitly described in the caption. E: Real CT panel from the TOF case showing collateral vascular anatomy; the caption identifies major aortopulmonary collateral arteries. F: CT angiographic reconstruction from a newborn with TOF; the caption explicitly identifies major aortopulmonary collateral arteries and a detectable left coronary artery. G: Real cardiac CT...

panels.figure_caption: CCT in a 2-day-old newborn with Tetralogy of Fallot, scanned in sedation and free-breathing at high heart rate (145 bpm), using a low-dose protocol (80 kV) and prospective ECG triggering. The main features are also detected and depicted in the images in multiplanar and curved reformation (MPR-CPR) and maximum intensity projection (MIP): ventricular septal defect and overriding aorta (black asterisk), PFO (black arrowhead), pulmonary valve atresia and pulmonary artery hypoplasia (white arrow), and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (white asterisks). Despite the very high heart rate, in a low-birth-weight preterm baby (2.3 Kg) scanned at a high heart rate, the left coronary artery is detectable (white arrowhead).
in_text_mentions: ul in both pre- and postoperative assessments of TOF. CCT is invaluable in pre-surgical planning, enabling surgeons to obtain a clear roadmap of the heart’s complex anatomy before corrective surgery (Figure 3). It assists in choosing the appropriate surgical approach and minimising intraoperative risks. An innovative application of CCT in TOF management involves the integration of CT data with 3D printing technology [70].
